title: Income/balance/cashflow statements for SMR serve NuScale Power Corp's (US) financials instead of SMR Jewels Ltd's (India) -- the ticker collision realized as live wrong data
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/SMR/income (and /balance, /cashflow) -> FY2025(12/31) total_revenue=$31,479,000, operating_income=-$689,571,000, net_income=-$355,794,000, ordinary_shares_number=318,480,601, provider="openbb-mcp". Compare GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/SMR (same symbol, no exchange qualifier) -> provider="yfinance", symbol="SMR.BO", market_cap=INR 1.77bn, revenue_ttm=INR 4.32bn (432 cr), correctly resolving to the Indian entity.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/S2_SMR.json:552-1023 (income, symbol="SMR", provider openbb-mcp, USD-scale loss-making figures), :1030-1710 (balance, ordinary_shares_number 318,480,601 at line 1686), :1712-2342 (cashflow, same USD-scale figures), :239-546 (fundamentals, correctly INR/yfinance/SMR.BO); cross-checked against docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/S2_SMR.json:378-449 (financials_detail: standalone FY2026 Sales INR 432 cr, Net Profit INR 25 cr, Total Assets INR 86 cr, 18.65M shares) and :517-524 (trap T1: "'SMR' resolves to SMR Jewels Ltd... AND to NUSCALE POWER Corp... A bare 'SMR' query has no correct answer without an exchange qualifier") and manifest.json slots S2/P20 (the collision pair).
notes: Mechanism: the /fundamentals/{symbol} route and the /fundamentals/{symbol}/income|balance|cashflow routes disagree on which company 'SMR' means for the identical request. The top-level route (yfinance provider) correctly carries the BSE resolution (symbol becomes SMR.BO) through to its response. The three statement sub-routes (openbb-mcp provider) appear to re-resolve the bare ticker independently rather than reusing the already-established BSE identity, landing on the US collision partner (NuScale Power Corp, NYSE: SMR) instead. Consequence: a user or agent pulling up SMR Jewels' income statement, balance sheet or cash flow via this app sees a nuclear-reactor company's audited US financials -- hundreds of millions of dollars of losses, 300M+ shares outstanding -- labelled under a BSE SME jewellery distributor's symbol, with no error, warning or exchange mismatch signal anywhere in the response. This is money-relevant data shown as true for the wrong entity, the single worst-case realization of the exact collision risk the outside-truth pack flagged before any app data was even pulled. Smallest fix shape: the income/balance/cashflow routes must resolve through the same exchange-qualified identity (SMR.BO / bse_code 544774) that /fundamentals/{symbol} already establishes -- either by threading the resolved yahoo_symbol/exchange into the openbb-mcp lookup, or by having those routes call the resolver first instead of handing the bare symbol straight to a US-biased provider.

title: Shareholding pattern (promoter/FII/DII/public) is entirely blank for a BSE SME stock that has exactly one filed quarter, and the app has no fallback -- "the single most gameable number" is simply absent
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/S2_SMR.json:2365-2378 (empty shareholding response); outside cross-check docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/S2_SMR.json:320-341 (shareholding block: Jun-2026 quarter, promoter_pct=65.74, fii_pct=9.88, dii_pct=0.84, public_pct=23.55, all sourced from screener.in, as_of 2026-06-30 -- the ONLY shareholding pattern this company has ever filed, per the pack's own note that there is no prior quarter to compare)
notes: Mechanism: the /disclosures/shareholding route returns a genuinely empty result set (count=0) for a scrip whose sole filed SEBI shareholding pattern is readily available from screener.in and was filed three months ago, not a hard-to-reach historical filing. The app's only adjacent data is yfinance's held_percent_insiders (78.56%) / held_percent_institutions (6.58%) on the /fundamentals payload, which are a different regulatory concept from the SEBI promoter/FII/DII/public breakdown and do not substitute for it (78.56% insiders vs 65.74% promoter is not a rounding gap, it's a different definition). Consequence: for a product whose stated moat is data trust and whose own task brief calls promoter holding "the single most gameable number in an Indian small-cap," a brand-new BSE SME listing -- exactly the risk profile where this number matters most -- shows nothing at all, with no honest 'unavailable' framing distinguishing it from a stock that simply has thin coverage. Smallest fix shape: audit the shareholding-pattern ingestion path for BSE SME-board scrips specifically (this pattern likely differs in filing venue/format from mainboard NSE/BSE patterns the pipeline already handles correctly for other battery slots), since the data is unambiguously public and single-sourced.

title: Results/filing-calendar route hard-fails (502) for a BSE-only, SME-listed stock instead of surfacing the results date the app has every reason to know
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/disclosures/results?symbol=SMR -> HTTP 502 {"detail": "nse_direct: 'SMR' is not a known NSE instrument"}
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/S2_SMR.json:2439-2450; outside cross-check docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/S2_SMR.json:351-367 (latest_results: FY2026 audited results filed 2026-06-25, BSE NEWSID 8074b32b-27a8-4e6c-a4aa-64d0bccebd0e, half-yearly reporting cadence explicitly noted)
notes: Mechanism: identical failure pattern to the P7_JUMBO battery slot (DAT-P7-2) -- the results-calendar route is hardwired to an NSE-only provider ('nse_direct') with no BSE fallback, so any BSE-only listing (a large share of Indian nano/small-caps, and effectively ALL BSE SME names) gets a raw upstream not-found string surfaced as an opaque 502 instead of the BSE-sourced filing date the app's own announcements feed (which DOES work for this scrip, see the diff's last_3_announcements row) could in principle supply. Consequence: any panel or agent surfacing 'latest results' or a results calendar hard-errors for this name. Smallest fix shape: same as DAT-P7-2 -- gate the nse_direct call on exchange presence (fall back to a BSE-sourced results/filing date when resolve.exchange == 'BSE' and no NSE symbol exists) instead of letting the NSE provider's not-found error propagate as a 502. Confirms this is a systemic route defect, not a JUMBO-specific fluke.

title: eps_ttm and its derived pe_ttm are both badly wrong and contradict the app's own freshly-served net_income_ttm/shares_outstanding for the same symbol
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/SMR -> eps=5.58, pe_ratio=17.02509 (95.0/5.58=17.03, internally consistent with itself). Same payload also carries net_income_ttm=247,484,992 and shares_outstanding=18,653,743 -> 247484992/18653743=13.27, which does not match the reported eps field.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/S2_SMR.json:250 (pe_ratio), :259 (eps), :273 (net_income_ttm), :275 (shares_outstanding); outside cross-check docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/S2_SMR.json:153-160 (pe_ttm: screener.in 7.16 vs stockanalysis.com 5.63, both computed from EPS 16.89) and :234-250 (eps_ttm: 16.89 on BOTH outside sources, explicitly flagged as pre-IPO share-count basis; pack's own post-IPO-adjusted estimate is ~13.3, which is close to the app's own internal 13.27 computation but far from the app's reported 5.58)
notes: Mechanism: identical failure pattern to P7_JUMBO's DAT-P7-3 -- the app's headline eps/pe fields are self-consistent with each other but disagree with BOTH outside-truth sources AND with the app's own already-fetched net_income_ttm/shares_outstanding, strongly suggesting eps (and hence the derived pe_ratio) is sourced from a stale or differently-scoped yfinance info-dict field rather than computed from the financial-statement data the app already holds in the same response. Consequence: a user sees a PE of 17.0x for a stock two independent outside sources price at 5.6x-7.2x (already a known 27% source disagreement, which the app's third, unrelated figure only compounds), and an EPS less than a third of the published/adjusted figures -- money-relevant valuation inputs shown as true when both are wrong. Smallest fix shape: same as DAT-P7-3 -- recompute eps from net_income_ttm/shares_outstanding (or reconcile against it with a tolerance check) instead of trusting the raw yfinance info-dict eps field; recompute pe_ratio from the corrected eps.

title: roce has no field anywhere in the fundamentals schema, despite roe being present and correct
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/SMR -> roe:0.66652 present and correct; no "roce" key exists anywhere in the response.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/S2_SMR.json:264 (roe present), (grep for "roce" across the full file returns zero matches -- no key at any point); outside cross-check docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/S2_SMR.json:183-190 (roce=71.5%, single clean screener.in source, no cross-source disagreement unlike pe_ttm)
notes: Mechanism: same gap as P7_JUMBO's DAT-P7-4, but narrower here since ROE itself is present and matches outside truth -- ROCE specifically is not modelled as a concept anywhere in the fundamentals schema. Consequence: a commonly screener.in-checked profitability ratio is entirely unavailable in the terminal, against a stated benchmark that has it cleanly, single-sourced. Smallest fix shape: add a computed ROCE (EBIT / (total assets - current liabilities), or from the already-fetched balance-sheet ingredients) as a fallback field, the same way debt_to_equity is apparently already computed/sourced correctly.

title: revenue_growth is blank where a single, clean, sourced YoY figure exists outside
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/SMR -> revenue_growth:null (field_meta: status="unavailable", reason="provider did not publish this field").
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/S2_SMR.json:276 (revenue_growth:null), :503-509 (field_meta.revenue_growth); outside cross-check docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/S2_SMR.json:218-224 (revenue_growth_yoy=64.3%, basis: FY2026 sales INR 432cr vs FY2025 INR 263cr standalone, matching screener.in's own TTM growth tile)
notes: Mechanism: yfinance's revenue_growth field is unpublished for this scrip, and the app has no computed fallback despite already holding both years' revenue figures (revenue_ttm is present and correct in the same payload; the prior year's figure is available via the /income route, even accounting for the entity-collision bug in DAT-S2-1). Consequence: a basic, uncontested growth metric that screener.in surfaces cleanly is simply missing. Smallest fix shape: compute revenue_growth_yoy from consecutive annual revenue figures when the provider field is null, the same pattern needed for the roce/roe fallback in DAT-S2-5.

title: Dividend paid-trailing-12m-per-share and yield are both blank where outside truth has a clean, unambiguous sourced 0/0% value
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/SMR -> dividend_per_share_ttm:null, dividend_yield:null (field_meta on both: status="unavailable", reason="provider did not publish this field").
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/S2_SMR.json:257-258 (dividend_yield, dividend_per_share at fundamentals-level), :281 (dividend_per_share_ttm), :370-383 (field_meta for both); outside cross-check docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/S2_SMR.json:290-291 (paid_trailing_12m_per_share=0, yield=0.0, both sourced from screener.in's Dividend Payout row reading -0% for every year FY2023-FY2026, corroborated by BSE CorporateAction returning zero dividend records)
notes: Mechanism: same gap as P7_JUMBO's DAT-P7-5, but cleaner here -- there is no caveat or staleness risk in the outside value (this company has unambiguously never paid a dividend, confirmed by two independent sources), yet the app renders null rather than a real, confirmed 0. Consequence: a user cannot distinguish 'no dividend data collected' from 'this company has genuinely never paid a dividend' -- both look identical (blank) in the app, when the correct, sourced answer is a clean, informative zero. Smallest fix shape: when the provider omits these fields outright and the app can independently confirm zero corporate actions of type dividend, surface a real computed 0/0.0% rather than collapsing to null; at minimum, distinguish 'provider silent' from 'confirmed never paid' in field_meta.

title: App has no concept of listing_date, so it cannot caveat that its own "fifty_two_week_high/low" fields describe 14 weeks of history, not 52
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/resolve?q=SMR and http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/SMR -> neither response contains a listing_date/IPO-date field anywhere; fifty_two_week_high=115.0 and fifty_two_week_low=75.85 are both correct values but carry no per-field as-of date beyond the generic provider query timestamp (2026-09-19T10:01:30), not the actual dates those extremes occurred.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/S2_SMR.json:11-61 (resolve body, no listing_date field), :239-546 (fundamentals body, full field list, no listing_date key), :261-262 (fifty_two_week_high/low values), :398-411 (field_meta for both, as_of is the query timestamp only); outside cross-check docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/S2_SMR.json:75-80 (listing_date=2026-06-08) and :294-300 (week52 block, explicit warning: "CRITICAL: the label '52-week' is a lie for this scrip -- it has only existed for 14 weeks... A terminal that renders a 52-week range band here implies 52 weeks of price discovery that never happened", corroborated by trap T8 at line ~562)
notes: Mechanism: the app's fifty_two_week_high/low VALUES are correct (verified against outside truth, no staleness skew between the two legs), so this is not a value-accuracy defect -- it is that the app holds no listing_date/IPO-date fact anywhere in its schema for this or any Indian equity slot inspected, so it has no way to know this particular 52-week field is describing a scrip that IPO'd 102 days ago. Consequence: any UI or agent narration built on 'fifty_two_week_high/low' for a recent listing implies a full year of price discovery that does not exist, exactly the trap the outside-truth pack flags as its most severe labelling risk for this name. Smallest fix shape: source listing_date/first-trade-date from the exchange (BSE's own listing announcement, already the same feed the app's working announcements route pulls from) and use it to gate/caveat 52-week-range presentation for recently listed names (e.g. render 'since listing' instead of '52-week' when history is under 52 weeks).

title: identity.board (SME vs mainboard classification) and face_value (par value) are both absent from the app's schema for this Indian equity
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/resolve?q=SMR and http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/SMR -> neither response contains a board/group/SME field or a face_value/par-value field anywhere.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/S2_SMR.json:11-61 (resolve body, no board or face_value field), :239-546 (fundamentals body, full field list, neither key present); outside cross-check docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/S2_SMR.json:55-61 (board="SME", BSE Group "M", source BSE ComHeader) and :265-271 (face_value=10.0 INR, corroborated by screener.in and ipowatch.in)
notes: Mechanism: same root cause as P7_JUMBO's DAT-P7-6 (yfinance does not carry either field for Indian scrips, and the BSE ComHeader feed already used for isin/bse_code is not consulted for board or face_value), but board/SME status is more consequential here than a systemic face_value gap alone: this is a BSE SME listing with a 2,000-share minimum lot size (INR ~1.9 lakh at current price) and thin liquidity (session volume peaking around 2,500 shares per the pack's intraday_liquidity_note) -- a user with no indication this is an SME-board name has no signal about that risk profile. Consequence: a demanding owner comparing against screener.in (which clearly labels SME board status) would immediately notice both gaps. Smallest fix shape: extend the BSE ComHeader ingestion already used for isin/bse_code/legal_name to also carry Group/board classification and face value through to the resolve/fundamentals response.
